messages.author: d12379035be5c6f9
messages.subject: 3D Home Range
parts:
Hi,
hope y'all are doing well. I am looking to estimate vulture's 3D home range. I wonder if someone has a working code example for this using ctmm package.

Thanks in advance. All the best,

Adrian

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: 3D Home Range
parts:
Hi Adrian,

As we have yet to publish a paper on the methods, these aren't well maintained features of the package, but if you run into any issues then feel free to submit a support request and I will fix it.

The extra ingredient you need over a 2D AKDE is a fitted movement model for vertical axis. You can do this by running most methods like variogram() and ctmm.select() with axes="z" instead of the default axes=c("x","y").

After you have the 2D movement model and the vertical movement model, you supply both to the akde() function in the CTMM and VMM arguments.

Plotting methods are not yet coded up for 3D UDs.

Best,
Chris

Hi Chris,

I am trying to fit a VMM, when I try to use axes="z" in ctmm.select() the unused argument (axes = "z") error message. This is the chunk of code I am using

svf.h<-variogram(v1, axes="z")
variogram.fit(svf.h)
FIT<-ctmm.select(v1,GUESS,axes="z",trace = T)
Error in ctmm.fit(data, GUESS, trace = trace2, ...) : 
  unused argument (axes = "z")

I wonder if it is related to package version, I am using 0.5.9. Thanks, Best!!
Adrian

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: 3D Home Range
parts:
Hi Adrian,

axes is not an argument of ctmm.select().  That information should be stored in the guess object and having an additional argument would be redundant. Also, I would use ctmm.guess() instead of variogram.fit(). It has more features.

Please do report any issues you come across with the vertical models. They are not tested regularly.

Best,
Chris
